answer: Seeded k-core membership resists sybils: an identity counts only if it sits in the k-core of the non-kin attestation graph anchored to a trusted seed — it needs at least k independent honest neighbors inside that core. A hollow block of sybils can forge dense internal edges, but they are worthless: the cluster attaches to the honest atlas across only a thin ridge of real edges, and no member can reach the required k honest in-core vouchers. Coreness bootstraps from the seed outward, so headcount inside the clique never manufactures membership — only scarce honest edges into the core do.
